review_notes: I read the whole file. It has two theorems: an iff characterizing injectivity of `Finsupp.mapDomain`, and a left-inverse characterization for the degree/support-card grouping. Neither is a simp-normal-form candidate. The first is a disjunctive characterization with an explicit `f` argument and a `Subsingleton` disjunct, so it is not a good simp lemma. The second is specific to `Fin 2` and one concrete map. The file has no simp attributes and no local simp-set definitions. Its proofs use `simp only` with explicit lemmas (`mapDomain_single`, `degree_single`, `support_single`, `card_singleton`, `false_or`), so I found no competing rules, unwanted expansion or cycle risk. I checked Mathlib's `mapDomain_injective` and `degree_single` in Mathlib/Data/Finsupp. They already cover the single-coefficient and degree computations the proofs use. I did not run Lean, so there is some uncertainty about simp behaviour in downstream files that I did not search.
